notes_for_us: Every team-objective row in the system - spawn-teambase, control-zone, capture-zone, boundary-shrinking - is filed under Shooter. A melee team game fighting over territory is a common Roblox shape and has to borrow all of its structure from a genre it is not, which the catalogue permits but the genre index gives no hint of.

'Many roles to play as' is the kind of statement step 0 calls a rule that implies a place - roles often need spawn rooms, class stations or equipment racks - but it is equally often a pure menu. I could not tell, and there is no guidance on which way to lean when a mechanic may or may not have a spatial footprint.

Action's presets are all free-for-all or PvE. There is no team-versus-team preset in the genre, so the closest match was Battlegrounds with its shape replaced, which is close to the 'no longer recognisable' line the skill warns about.

notes_for_us: Keeping the whole preset costs a route here: reveal-exit is P3 and nothing else in the build is, so a school-corridor story game is routed as an interior-exterior transition purely because the Story preset carries a cinematic vista. This is the clearest instance of preset padding in the batch and it is visible in the pipeline, not just the option list.

A choice-driven story game is mostly a set of rooms where scripted scenes happen. Nothing in the system marks a place as a scene location, so the teacher's office and the lunch table - the two places the whole plot turns on - are indistinguishable from any other room in the handoff.

Adventure's shapes all assume a journey through space. A story that moves through time in one building had to reach the catalogue for interior-single, and the Story preset's chapter gates then had to be reinterpreted as doors inside a school.

About 90% of this 400-word prompt is narrative that is neither layout nor mechanics in the step 0 sense - it is a script. mechanics absorbed it because there is nowhere else, which makes that array a dumping ground rather than a handoff to the gameplay stream.

notes_for_us: Extreme-sports trick games fall between three genres and land in none of them cleanly. Racing excludes them by its own boundary note (no lap, no finish), Sports assumes a scored field, and Simulation takes them by default into a preset built for cart rides and ragdolls. Skate, BMX and MX games are a large Roblox category to be routed by exclusion.

physics-rig is the only row for a ramp and its wording is about contraptions whose reactions are the entertainment. A skatepark is not a contraption - it is a designed set of takeoffs and landings with sightlines and run-ups between them, and that is the whole map here.

Eight brand names are a concrete, checkable request and there is nowhere for them but mechanics. The same is true of the trick list. Neither is layout, but both are the sort of thing a user will judge the result on.
